newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Gilt, short sterling vols slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Gilt, short sterling vols slightly lower.

text.p: Implied volatility levels on gilts and short sterling options traded on LIFFE were down slightly on Wednesday, traders said.
A batch of jobs and earnings data was widely seen as pointing to a possible need for interest rate rises in the medium term, but had little effect on implied vols, they said.

"The approach of the UK budget (on November 26) is sure to keep the market bid up in terms of implied volatility, so I don't think we will see anything lower than what we have now," said Mark Robinson, a futures and options broker for HSBC Futures.

Robinson said that in the run up to November 26 he expected a small move up in implied volatility, probably in the gilt market more than short sterling, with some sell-off possible thereafter depending on the budget's contents.
Wednesday's data showed unemployment tumbling to a five-and-a-half year low of 7.2 percent in October and wage cost growth up to 5.2 percent in the three months to September.
Robinson said it was not surprising volatility levels had softened only slightly after the numbers.
"In general terms volatility is probably still low anyway. Sterling has not been particularly bid but it has been up a little over the last couple of days."
Implied volatility on December short sterling puts was quoted at about 11.4 percent, down from around 11.5 percent at Wednesday's opening.
Another trader said short sterling puts were most in demand after the data, especially December 93.50 puts. LIFFE screen data showed 3,270 lots traded.
The trader said the December 110-00 gilt calls were popular, with implied volatility at 7.5 percent -- compared with 7.27 percent at Tuesday's close.
Robinson said December gilt options were "starting to get a bit erratic" because they had only nine days left to expiry.
"As a guide, an at-the-money 109-00 strike will be trading about 7.5 pct in terms of vol and this compares with opening levels around 7.75 per cent," he said.
